# ask


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

`ask` answers a question from the vault with a language model.
[Urai](https://github.com/vedicreader/urai) is the chat library that
vishalakshi calls. [Rishi](https://github.com/vedicreader/rishi)
provides the model backends, and Urai registers them the first time a
chat is built.

A model id names the model, and the id selects the backend. The local
backends are LiteRT, MLX, llama.cpp and Ollama. A hosted API id looks
like `claude/sonnet` or `gpt-4.1-nano`.

With no id, the vault uses `gemma-4-E2B`. This small model runs on this
machine through LiteRT and needs no API key. Set `$VISHALAKSHI_MODEL` to
use a different default.

LiteRT is asked for the GPU backend. When no GPU is available, LiteRT
uses its default backend and a warning appears. Set `$VISHALAKSHI_GPU=0`
to keep LiteRT on the CPU.

`chat_kw=` passes any other chat constructor argument, such as a
temperature.

### Answering with citations

`ask(question)` calls `context` to retrieve the sections of the vault
that best match the question.
[`mk_prompt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#mk_prompt)
numbers the sections \[1\], \[2\] and so on. It also lists the related
sections by title only. A related section is a neighbour of a retrieved
section in vector similarity. The question does not retrieve it.

The system prompt `VAULT_SP` tells the model to answer only from the
sections and to cite the number of each section it used. `ask` returns
the answer and
[`cited`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cited).
[`cited`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cited)
lists the sections that the answer cites. Each entry has a `node_id`
that `read` opens.

The context budget is `sections=4` and `max_chars=1500`. `max_chars` is
the number of characters kept from each section.

To ask about particular documents, pass `ref=` with one or more
documents, or use `ask_doc` from [extract](06_extract.ipynb).
`doc_context` then puts the named documents first, whole, as sections
\[1\] to \[n\]. The named documents share `doc_chars` characters.
`doc_context` adds `related` sections from the rest of the vault after
them.

*Return the prompt line that names which numbered sections are the
documents asked about.*

`mk_chat=` gives `ask` a chat that the host already runs, such as a
model that an app has loaded. `ask` then builds no new chat. The privacy
check reads the runtime of the chat that `ask` uses. A hosted chat
passed by mistake is treated as hosted.

A section is private in three cases. The detector finds personal
identifiers in it. Its document is marked as personal. Its document has
a level above Open for another reason, such as the document type or the
shelf floor.

Before `ask` sends anything, it drops each related section that holds
personal information. When `ref=` names documents, it also drops each
retrieved section that holds personal information. `pii=` then sets what
happens to the remaining sections:

<table>

<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th><code>pii=</code></th>
<th>what happens when the sections are private</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>local</code></td>
<td>A model on this machine answers. The model is
<code>pii_model</code>, else <code>$VISHALAKSHI_PII_MODEL</code>, else
the default model. It runs under <code>PII_SP</code>, a system prompt
that forbids repeating any personal detail. If that chat is not local,
<code>ask</code> sends nothing and the answer says so.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>redact</code></td>
<td><code>ask</code> masks the recognised identifiers in the text,
heading line, title and source of each section. The model named by
<code>model=</code> then answers, hosted or not.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>refuse</code></td>
<td>No model is asked. The answer says what was held back.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The default policy is `local` when a local runtime is installed, and
`redact` when none is. `pii='off'` is not valid for `ask`. It gives a
warning and applies the default. The `policy` field of the result names
the policy that ran.

Under every policy, a hosted model receives a Local only section as the
bare line `[n] [withheld: local only]`. The line has no heading, title
or source. `send_check` below explains the rule.

Under `redact`, `ask` does not mask a name that has no title before it,
such as Dr. Name detection is on by default (`pii_ner=True`).

`ask` scans each answer over private sections again before it returns
the answer. It masks any identifier that the model repeated, and
`leaked` lists the kinds of identifier.

The result also has the `prompt` and the `context` that the model read.
Under `local` they hold the private sections whole. A host that gives
the result to a hosted model must pass on only `answer` and
[`cited`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cited).

## Deciding what a model may be sent

`send_check` runs before anything goes to a model. For each document,
page or piece of text, it decides one of three outcomes: whole, masked,
or withheld. Withheld means not sent.

`send_check` returns the decisions in `rows`, and the subsets `send`,
`masked` and `withheld`. It also returns a `why` sentence for a person
to read before the send. An example is
`gpt-4.1-nano, hosted. 1 personal document masked, 1 document open, 1 local-only document withheld.`

[`send_rule`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#send_rule)
holds the rule:

- A model on this machine receives everything whole.
  [`model_local`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#model_local)
  decides which models are local. LiteRT, MLX and llama.cpp are always
  local. Ollama is local only when `$OLLAMA_HOST` points at this
  machine. Every other runtime is hosted. A chat that names no runtime
  is hosted.
- An Open item goes whole to any model.
- A Local only item is withheld from a hosted model under every policy.
  `allow=True` does not change this.
- Under `redact`, a Personal item goes to a hosted model masked. Under
  `local` and `refuse`, it is withheld.
- A page image cannot be masked. A Personal page image is withheld from
  a hosted model under every policy except `off`, and when `allow=True`.
- `allow=True` allows once. It sends Personal items whole for that one
  call, as `policy='off'` does.

`ask`, `explain`, `categorize`, `extract`,
[`read_doc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_doc),
`reparse` and `proofread` all decide through this rule. The decision
covers everything that goes with the text. A document’s title, headings
and source path are masked or withheld with it. A page image is read
with the document’s title in its prompt. `send_check` judges the title
with the page.

`build_graph` sends every chunk to its chat with nothing to mask.
`connect` calls `build_graph`. A hosted chat builds the graph only when
every document on the shelf is Open. Otherwise `build_graph` sends
nothing and the result says why.

Masking replaces only what the detector recognises. A document marked
Personal by hand, with nothing recognisable in it, goes to a hosted
model under `redact` exactly as stored.

The `send_log` table of the vault records each send to a hosted model. A
row has the time, the document and pages, the model and runtime, the
policy, and the kinds of personal information when known. `sends(ref)`
reads the log, newest first. The log has no row for a send to a local
model or for a withheld item.

### Vault.ask

``` python
def ask(
    question:str, # what you want to know
    ref:NoneType=None, # documents to ask about: a doc_id, source, title or path, or a list of them
    schema:NoneType=None, # answer as this shape instead of prose: a SCHEMAS key, dataclass, or 'field:type' spec
    model:str=None, # an id, a path, `mlx/…`; None -> $VISHALAKSHI_MODEL
    chat_kw:dict=None, # anything else Urai's `Chat` takes: temp, runtime, think, …
    sections:int=4, # operative sections retrieved
    related:int=6, # associative sections offered as leads
    kind:str=None, # restrict retrieval to one or more KINDS
    code:int=None, # code sections to add; None -> 4 if kosha has indexed the repo
    dir:str=None, # repo for the code legs; None -> the cwd repo
    max_chars:int=1500, # chars of each retrieved section shown to the model
    doc_chars:int=8000, # chars of `ref`'s documents shown to the model, shared between them
    sp:str="You answer questions from a personal research vault.\n\nYou are given numbered sections retrieved from the user's own corpus: papers, web pages,\ntranscripts, files and their own notes. Answer only from those sections.\n\nRules:\n- Cite every claim with the bracketed number of the section it came from, like [2]. A sentence\n  drawing on two sections cites both.\n- If the sections do not answer the question, say exactly what is missing rather than filling the\n  gap from memory. A vault that admits a hole is useful; one that guesses is not.\n- Sections marked RELATED were reached by association, not by matching the question. Use them for\n  context or to point somewhere worth reading next, and say so when you do.\n- Prefer the user's own notes when they conflict with a source, and flag the disagreement.", # system prompt
    mk_chat:NoneType=None, # build chats with this instead of `new_chat`; same signature
    pii:str=None, # local|redact|refuse; None -> local when a local runtime exists, else redact
    pii_model:str=None, # the local model that answers then; None -> $VISHALAKSHI_PII_MODEL
    pii_ner:bool=True, # also look for names that follow a title such as Dr; a pattern, not a model
    instruction:str='', # an instruction from the questioner, for a second turn
    stale:bool=False, # include retained pages beyond the file's current end
    **kw
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict: # forwarded to Vault.context
```

*Answer a question from the vault, or about the documents `ref` names,
citing the numbered sections the answer used.*

### Recording what a model said

[`CachedChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cachedchat)
records the replies of a model on disk and plays them back. Tests and
these pages use it to show real answers without a model run. The vault
treats a
[`CachedChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cachedchat)
as any other chat.

The recording folder is `path`, else `$VISHALAKSHI_CHAT_CACHE`, else
`chatcache` in the working directory.

A question with no recording raises an error. When
`$VISHALAKSHI_RECORD_CHAT` is set, the question goes to the real model
and
[`CachedChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cachedchat)
records the reply. The next run answers from disk.

Building a
[`CachedChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cachedchat)
registers Rishi’s runtimes, as
[`new_chat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#new_chat)
does. `runtime` then names the backend of the id and builds no engine.

``` python
import subprocess, sys
```

The default budget is `sections=4` and `max_chars=1500`. Six sections of
4,000 characters each overflowed the context window of the 2B default
model. LiteRT reported this as a send failure with no explanation
(`evals/RESULTS.md`).

When a send fails this way, `ask` gives a warning and tries once more on
a new chat. The second try uses the first two sections, each cut to a
third of `max_chars`, and no related sections.

## Try it

Retrieval needs no model. Only the answer needs one.
[`mk_prompt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#mk_prompt)
builds the exact text that the model reads. The cell below prints one
prompt.

``` python
v = Vault(':memory:')
v.note('Late chunking beats naive chunking because context survives the split.')
print(mk_prompt('why late chunking?', v.context('late chunking'))[:400])
```

``` python
# a document to ask about becomes section [1] in full, and the rest of the vault follows it
_dc = _v.doc_context('doc 3', 'rank fusion', related=2)
test_eq(_dc.results[0].breadcrumb, 'doc 3')
test_eq(_dc.results[0].text, _v.document('doc 3').text)             # the whole document, not a chunk
assert all(r.doc_id != _dc.doc.doc_id for r in _dc.results[1:])     # never the document itself twice
test_eq(len(_v.doc_context('doc 3', 'rank fusion', max_chars=200).results[0].text), 200)
assert mk_prompt('rank fusion', _dc, note=_dc.note).endswith(_dc.note + 'Question: rank fusion')

# several docs: each is a numbered section; max_chars is a shared window
_dc2 = _v.doc_context(['doc 3', 'doc 5'], 'rank fusion', related=2, max_chars=600)
test_eq(_dc2.results.attrgot('breadcrumb')[:2], ['doc 3', 'doc 5'])
test_eq([len(r.text) for r in _dc2.results[:2]], [300, 300])
assert all(r.doc_id not in set(_dc2.docs.attrgot('doc_id')) for r in _dc2.results[2:])
test_eq(len(_dc2.results), 4)                                       # 2 named + related=2
assert '[1]–[2] are the documents' in _dc2.note, _dc2.note
test_eq(doc_note(1)[:19], '[1] is the document')
```

``` python
res = L([AttrDict(node_id='d#1', title='A', breadcrumb='A › B', filename='f', doc_id='d')])
test_eq(cited('as [1] shows, and again [1], but not [9]', res).attrgot('node_id'), ['d#1'])
```

``` python
# reasoning: full pair, truncated opener, or MLX closing-only tag
test_eq(split_reasoning('<think>weighing [1]</think>\n\nRRF fuses ranks [2].'),
        ('RRF fuses ranks [2].', 'weighing [1]'))
test_eq(split_reasoning('weighing [1]</think>\n\nRRF fuses ranks [2].'),
        ('RRF fuses ranks [2].', 'weighing [1]'))
test_eq(split_reasoning('RRF fuses ranks [2].'), ('RRF fuses ranks [2].', ''))
# a section the reasoning weighed and dropped must not come back as a citation
test_eq(cited(split_reasoning('cites [1]</think> cites nothing')[0], res), [])
```

## When the sections hold personal information

[pii](09_pii.ipynb) explains the detector and the marks. The cells below
show what `ask` does with them. They use a stand-in chat that records
everything it receives. A leak appears as a recorded call.

The check runs on the chat that `ask` built, before `ask` sends
anything. The next cell passes a hosted chat under the default `local`
policy. `ask` does not call the model.

``` python
_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?', mk_chat=_chat('remote', 'THIS MUST NEVER BE SENT'))
test_eq(_seen, {})                       # the model was never called at all
test_eq(r.refused, True)
r.answer
```

    'held back: these sections hold personal information (card, email, phone) and remote is not a local runtime, so nothing was sent to it'

With a local runtime, `ask` sends the private sections to the local
model under `PII_SP`. `PII_SP` tells the model to answer with counts,
kinds and totals instead of personal details, and to say what it held
back.

``` python
_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?', mk_chat=_chat('litert',
    'One invoice, 240.00 GBP, due in September. Holding back the name, email, phone and card. '
    'Tell me what you need: a total, a due date, or a yes/no.'))
test_eq(_seen['runtime'], 'litert')
test_eq(_seen['sp'], PII_SP)             # not VAULT_SP: that one tells it to cite, and a citation points at the text
test_eq(r.get('refused', False), False)
r.answer
```

    'One invoice, 240.00 GBP, due in September. Holding back the name, email, phone and card. Tell me what you need: a total, a due date, or a yes/no.'

`instruction=` sends a follow-up turn. When the local model holds
something back, it names an instruction that would let it answer, such
as “give me the total and the due date”. The caller sends that
instruction with the same question.

``` python
_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?', instruction='Give me the total and the due date only.',
           mk_chat=_chat('litert', 'Total 240.00 GBP, due 2026-09-01.'))
test_eq('Instruction from the questioner' in _seen['prompt'], True)
r.answer
```

    'Total 240.00 GBP, due 2026-09-01.'

`ask` scans every answer over private sections again before it returns
the answer. It masks identifiers that the model repeated, and `leaked`
lists their kinds.

``` python
_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?',
           mk_chat=_chat('litert', 'It is for ada@example.com, card 4111 1111 1111 1111.'))
test_eq(r.answer, 'It is for [EMAIL], card [CARD].')
r.leaked
```

    {'email': 1, 'card': 1}

`pii='redact'` masks the recognised identifiers in the text of each
section. A hosted model then answers. A name is masked only when a title
such as Dr comes before it. “Ada Lovelace” is not masked, as a
real-model cell further down shows.

``` python
_seen.clear()
r = _v.ask('what is on invoice 4471?', pii='redact', mk_chat=_chat('remote', 'An invoice for 240.00 GBP [1]'))
test_eq('ada@example.com' in _seen['prompt'], False)
test_eq(_seen['runtime'], 'remote')
r.answer
```

    'An invoice for 240.00 GBP [1]'

`ask` scrubs the fields of a structured answer (`schema=`) in the same
way. An API key counts as personal information, as an email address
does. A hosted chat is refused for a section that holds an API key, and
for a document marked by hand.

``` python
import inspect
```

## Against real models

These cells replay replies that
[`CachedChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cachedchat)
recorded from real models. They run without the models. Each cell shows
one rule or one way a call can fail.

The vault holds nothing private here. The default local model on its
default backend answers and cites section \[1\].

``` python
r = model_ask(open_vault, q)
test_eq((r.model, r.runtime), (dflt_model, 'litert'))   # gemma-4-E2B on LiteRT, unasked for
test_eq(r.pii.has_pii, False)                           # nothing private: one model, VAULT_SP, no scrubbing
test_eq(r.cited.attrgot('n'), [1])                      # it cited [1]...
assert r.cited[0]['node_id'], r.cited                   # ...and [1] resolves to a section of the vault
r.answer
```

    'Reciprocal rank fusion combines rankings from legs that share no vector space by summing $1/(60 + \\text{rank})$ over the legs [1].'

The same question goes to a hosted model. Only the model id changes.

``` python
r = model_ask(open_vault, q, model=CLOUD)
test_eq((r.model, r.runtime), (CLOUD, 'remote'))
test_eq(r.pii.has_pii, False)                           # ...which is the only reason it was allowed to run
test_eq(r.cited.attrgot('n'), [1])
assert r.cited[0]['node_id'], r.cited
r.answer
```

    'Reciprocal rank fusion combines the rankings from different legs by summing the reciprocals of their ranks plus 60, specifically using the formula 1/(60 + rank) for each leg. A document that is ranked well in multiple legs will have a higher combined score, making it outperform documents that are only ranked well in a single leg [1].'

The vault holds an invoice. The local model answers under `PII_SP`.
`ask` scans the answer again before it returns it.

``` python
r = model_ask(private_vault, pq)
test_eq(sorted(r.pii.identifying), ['card', 'email', 'phone'])
test_eq((r.model, r.runtime), (pii_model_, 'litert'))   # local, so it answered rather than refusing
test_eq(r.get('refused', False), False)
# answer must not contain invoice PII; r.leaked says model vs scrubber
for s in ('ada@example.com', '4111 1111 1111 1111', '020 7946 0958', 'Ada Lovelace'): assert s not in r.answer, (s, r.answer)
r.answer, r.get('leaked')
```

    ('I am holding back the specific personal details from the invoice.\nThe invoice is for an amount of 240.00 GBP, due on 2026-09-01.',
     None)

Under `pii='local'`, a hosted `model=` does not receive private
sections. The local `pii_model` answers instead. A hosted model named as
`pii_model` also receives nothing. The check sees a hosted chat and
refuses.

``` python
# naming a hosted model where the sections are private routes to the local one instead
test_eq(model_ask(private_vault, pq, model=CLOUD).runtime, 'litert')

r = model_ask(private_vault, pq, model=CLOUD, pii_model=CLOUD)   # ...and naming it as the *local* one is refused
test_eq((r.refused, r.runtime, r.answer.startswith('held back')), (True, 'remote', True))
# nothing was sent, and the proof is that there is nothing to replay: a call would have been
# recorded under one of these two keys, and neither is in the cache
_c = ch_fn(CLOUD).cache
for _sp in (VAULT_SP, PII_SP): assert f'{CLOUD}|call|{_sp}|{r.prompt}' not in _c
r.answer
```

    'held back: these sections hold personal information (card, email, phone) and remote is not a local runtime, so nothing was sent to it'

`pii='redact'` masks the identifiers, and a hosted model answers. “Ada
Lovelace” has no title before it. The detector does not mask it, and it
reaches the hosted model.

``` python
r = model_ask(private_vault, pq, model=CLOUD, pii='redact')
test_eq((r.model, r.runtime, r.get('refused', False)), (CLOUD, 'remote', False))
test_eq('[CARD]' in r.prompt and '[EMAIL]' in r.prompt, True)   # what the network actually carried
for s in ('ada@example.com', '4111 1111 1111 1111', '020 7946 0958'):
    assert s not in r.prompt, s
assert 'Ada Lovelace' in r.prompt          # ...and the limit of it, pinned rather than discovered
r.answer
```

    'Invoice 4471 is for Ada Lovelace, with contact details including email and phone number. It shows an amount of 240.00 GBP, due on 2026-09-01, and the payment is to be made using a card ending in [CARD] (specific digits not provided) [1].'

The follow-up turn with `instruction=`, against the real local model.

``` python
r = model_ask(private_vault, pq, instruction='Give me the amount and the due date only, and no name.')
assert 'Instruction from the questioner' in r.prompt
test_eq((r.runtime, r.get('refused', False)), ('litert', False))
for s in ('ada@example.com', '4111 1111 1111 1111', '020 7946 0958'): assert s not in r.answer, s
r.answer
```

    'Amount: 240.00 GBP, Due Date: 2026-09-01.'
